removal_suggestion: The tree implication cannot be removed while retaining both the immutable m = n − 1 value and the guarantee that every facility is connected. Re-present the connectivity guarantee instead: guarantee only that all core facilities are in one connected component, while allowing non-core facilities to be disconnected. Then the component containing the cores may contain cycles despite m = n − 1.

common_affordance: The input graph is guaranteed connected and has exactly n − 1 edges, so it is a tree with unique paths

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DFS-based marking logic is incomplete for the required terminal-subtree computation and relies on a single rooted traversal rather than robustly aggregating all terminal-containing branches.

Its Kruskal/DSU approach applies an MST-style edge-selection heuristic instead of correctly computing the minimum subtree connecting exactly the core facilities, leading to incorrect terminal-connectivity decisions.

recommended_edit: Replace the guarantee that every facility can connect to every other facility with a guarantee only that all core facilities are mutually connected; explicitly allow other facilities or components to be disconnected. Keep m = n − 1 and all examples unchanged. This permits cycles in the core-containing component, defeating tree-only parent/order and pruning solutions.
